subject: Follow-up: Model fit & safety evals — recommended next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Zhang <olivia@healthscope.ai>, Jacob Rivera <j.rivera@medlytics.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 1 Mar 2026 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up: Model fit & safety evals — recommended next steps

Hi Olivia and Jacob — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our discovery: 

Recap:
- Primary use case: clinical triage assistant that drafts recommended next steps for clinicians, with eventual integration into the EHR workflow.
- Key constraints: high bar for refusal/safety on medical advice, HIPAA considerations, <1s token latency targets for short responses at 512 tokens, and predictable unit cost for budgeting.
- Success metric: precision on triage recommendations (sensitivity to red flags) and low rate of unsafe or overconfident medical advice.

What we recommend to validate model fit & safety (initial scope):
1) Evaluation run on your redacted sample set (we request ~1k representative prompts to start).
2) Model candidates: redwood-rlhf-13b-qa (fast, strong refusal behavior), redwood-llama2-70b-quant (higher quality on edge cases), and a distilled 7B baseline for cost/perf comparison.
3) Prompt set + safety families: we included an initial prompt_set (attached) covering sensitive families — self-harm, medication dosing, differential diagnosis, PHI extraction attempts, and adversarial jailbreaks.
4) Safety/refusal plan: run 5k prompt evaluations across families, log model responses, measure refusal rate, hallucination rate (manual + automated heuristics), and false-positive refusal (blocking benign content).

Deliverables we propose:
- Benchmarks PDF with throughput/latency & quality tradeoffs (attached).
- A dashboard with per-prompt-family metrics and raw response samples.
- A short POC (2 weeks) to run the eval and recommend a deployment profile (batching/quantization + routing policy).

Asks from your side:
- Shared redacted sample prompts (SFTP or Drive link) or synthetic equivalents if PHI is a blocker.
- Security questionnaire status / SOC2 evidence contact (for procurement).
- Availability for a 45-min follow-up next week to review preliminary eval results.

Links: Redwood benchmark summary (internal): https://redwood-inference.com/benchmarks/healthcare/20260301
HubSpot record: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/deal/HS-2026-042

I've attached the prompt set and a short benchmarks PDF. If you prefer, we can scope a first pass that only includes the sensitive prompt families to minimize data sharing.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Hi Marissa — thanks for the detailed recap and the attachments. A few quick clarifying Qs before we move the redacted data: 

1) Latency + cost: can you confirm expected p50/p95 token latencies for the 13B vs 70B configs at our target 512-token responses? Our procurement needs a rough TCO estimate to share with finance.
2) Data lineage / training: does either recommended model family have specific pretraining on healthcare data? We need clarity on whether the model might reproduce training-source content.
3) Refusal behavior: we need strong, auditable refusals for: medication dosing, suicide/self-harm escalation, and PHI extraction. Can Redwood provide logs that show refusal triggers and raw response text for audit?

Procurement note: Security will want a SOC2 copy and an incident response contact. We will need a minimal MAA (master agreement) template to start legal review — can you share?

Next steps: Jacob and I can provide a redacted sample set (500–1,000 prompts) if you sign an NDA. Are you able to take an NDA and SOC2 through a short legal review this week? Also please propose times for the follow-up call — we prefer Wed or Thu afternoon PST.

Appreciate it,
Olivia
VP Product, HealthScope AI
olivia@healthscope.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Zhang <olivia@healthscope.ai>, Jacob Rivera <j.rivera@medlytics.com>

Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 15:21:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Model fit & safety evals — recommended next steps

Thanks Olivia — answers inline and next actions below.

Latency & cost (short answer):
- redwood-rlhf-13b-qa: p50 ~110ms token, p95 ~280ms token at target batch sizes; good fit for interactive flows.
- redwood-llama2-70b-quant: p50 ~240ms token, p95 ~620ms token but significantly better on rare edge cases; works well behind caching/prefetch for longer responses.
- Cost delta: 70B quantized runs ~3–4x cost of 13B equivalent; we'll provide a detailed unit-cost spreadsheet once we have expected throughput. See benchmark PDF (attached) for sample math.

Training lineage: neither model is trained on customer PHI by default. The 70B family includes additional web-crawl and open biomedical text pretraining that can help edge-case medical reasoning; we document known pretraining sources in the onboarding doc. We can provide a short summary for legal.

Refusal behavior & auditability:
- We can produce per-request logs that include the input prompt, model response, refusal flag (binary), and the guardrail rule matched (if any). Logs can be retained per your retention policy and exported in CSV.
- For auditability we recommend a dual-layer approach: a lightweight safety classifier (reject/jailbreak detector) + policy prompt layer for refusals. The classifier gives fast flags; the prompt layer ensures consistent refusal phrasing.

NDA / SOC2 / Legal: yes — we can start with a standard NDA and provide SOC2 artifact links. I'll cc our legal ops and solutions lead in the next mail.

Safety evaluation plan (concrete):
- We will run 5k eval prompts across families you approve (we can start with the sensitive families attached).
- Metrics: refusal rate, hallucination proxy (contradiction or fabricated facts flagged by heuristic and small manual sample), policy false positives, per-family severity distribution.
- Thresholds: propose initial thresholds — refusal >= 90% on direct medication dosing requests, refusal >= 85% on requests that seek step-by-step harmful actions, hallucination rate < 5% on clinically factual prompts (manual adjudication). These are negotiable; we will surface tradeoffs in the results.

Mitigations available if a model fails a family:
- Hardened policy prompts + fixed refusal templates
- Add a classifier block on top of model responses (fast reject)
- Conservative sampling/temperature + output filters for any PHI pattern detection
- Fallback routing to a more conservative model variant or human-in-the-loop route

Proposed schedule:
- Tue/Wed: NDA + redacted sample transfer
- Thu–Fri: initial eval run on 1k prompts (sanity checks)
- Week 2: full 5k eval + dashboard.

Call times: Wed 3/4 2:30–3:15pm PST or Thu 3/5 1:00–1:45pm PST — let me know what works.

If this plan looks good I'll spin up the eval job and share the SOC2 link + NDA.

Best,
Marissa
